tools.name: coverage
tools.description: States loaded, procedure family keys by market segment, DME and prescribing categories, data years, and the caller's plan limits.

tools.name: glossary
tools.description: Definitions of the published metrics: unit, source, reported or estimated, caveat, backtested accuracy, and the current data year. Cite these when explaining a number.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search by name. Returns surgeons (npi), practices (pacId), hospitals and ASCs (ccn), device companies (company slug), states, metros (metro code) and counties (FIPS), for use in the other tools.

tools.name: rank_territory
tools.description: Surgeons operating in a place for a procedure family, ranked by Medicare cases weighted by how deep their payment ties to a device company are: cases and change, MA-adjusted trend, practice and employment, likely incumbent (the company most engaged with them, by Open Payments) and relationship depth

tools.name: new_surgeons
tools.description: Surgeons in a place the Medicare files cannot show yet: fellows who stayed (paid the assistant-at-surgery fee, now practising here) and recent joins of established groups. Each with its evidence and the signal's backtested accuracy.

tools.name: territory_changes
tools.description: Recent moves and practice changes among a territory's surgeons, and surgeons whose Medicare cases are placed here but who practise elsewhere now.

tools.name: incumbents
tools.description: Which device companies engage a territory's surgeons for a family and how deeply, surgeons open or lunch-only (no company over $500), independent-channel candidates, employment mix, where cases are done (hospital, ASC, office) and the main sites of care.

tools.name: market_outlook
tools.description: A family's market in a place: Medicare cases by year, the all-Medicare estimate, the forecast to 2030 with ranges, the 65+ population and its growth, and per-metro or per-county supply, access and demand index.

tools.name: surgeon_profile
tools.description: One clinician by NPI: Medicare cases by family and trend, cases under CMS's floor, forecast, peers, device payments by company and depth, research, practice and who decides, billing groups, sites, partners, movement, DME ordered, device-pointing prescribing, academic record, and the new-surgeon sign

tools.name: practice_profile
tools.description: A PECOS group practice by PAC ID: size, employment model and who decides, Medicare cases by family with its top surgeons, device payments by company, and sites.

tools.name: facility_profile
tools.description: A hospital or ASC by CMS certification number: payer mix, inpatient DRG and outpatient procedure volumes, ASC case counts, negotiated commercial and Medicare Advantage prices for the families done there, and who operates there.

tools.name: who_orders
tools.description: Clinicians ranked by referred DME a supplier billed (bracing, bone growth stimulators, CGM, pumps, NPWT, dressings, compression, CPAP, CPM) or by device-pointing prescribing (rx-insulin, rx-anticoagulant, rx-bph, rx-glaucoma, rx-overactive-bladder), with specialty mix.

tools.name: warm_paths
tools.description: Which of the rep's own customers (marked on MedaRep) can open a door to a surgeon: partners now or before, the same hospital, the same device company, or a partner in common, with each path's strength. Give one NPI, or a family and a place for the territory's warmest targets and its lookalikes: surg

tools.name: cross_sell
tools.description: More business in the accounts the rep already has: for each of their customers (marked on MedaRep), the procedures they do that one of the rep's lines covers (my_lines) where that line's company is not already the one most engaged with them for those products, with their Medicare cases, who engages

tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: A device company by name or slug: FDA 510(k), De Novo and PMA decisions by family and year, recalls (open first, by class), adverse-event trend against each family's category over two closed years, and consolidated financials for public parents. Needs the product and company coverage add-on; without

tools.name: family_coverage
tools.description: A procedure family's device landscape: the FDA product codes behind it, clearances in the last 24 months by firm, open recalls, and the category's adverse-event trend by firm. Needs the product and company coverage add-on; without it the answer is a notice.

tools.name: new_clearances
tools.description: A procedure family's new FDA 510(k), De Novo and PMA decisions from the last days (default 90), read weekly from FDA: each as a new entrant (the company's first here), a new system (a name it has not cleared before) or a line extension (more of a line it already sells), with the basis, what it means

tools.name: ownership_changes
tools.description: Dated deals that changed who sells device products: acquisitions, mergers, carve-outs (Stryker's US spinal implants to VB Spine), spin-offs and renames, each in a sentence with what it means for a rep and its source. Filter by company (as asked, as it reported, or its owner now), procedure family (c

tools.name: competitor_scorecard
tools.description: Device companies scored against the others in a procedure family on innovation pace (new FDA decisions, market entries), recall and report signals (recalls, MAUDE reports above the category), commercial momentum (share of the family's Medicare cases through surgeons they engage, this year against la

tools.name: switching
tools.description: Surgeons in a territory whose main device company for a family (the one most engaged with them for its products) changed between the last two Open Payments years: who, from whom, to whom, with their Medicare cases, plus new and ended ties. Needs the product and company coverage add-on.

tools.name: opportunities
tools.description: A territory's surgeons ranked by dated reasons they may be worth a call now: a recall or rising MAUDE reports at a company engaged with them for these products (possible supply or service disruption, not a finding of fault), a new FDA clearance for their main company (read as new entrant, new system

tools.name: my_lists
tools.description: The rep's prospect lists on MedaRep with counts by status, or one list (by id or name) with where each surgeon stands (target, contacted, trialing, using_us, competitor, lost, passed: the account's own stage, the same on every list), note, practice and latest Medicare cases.

tools.name: save_to_list
tools.description: Add surgeons by NPI to one of the rep's prospect lists (by id or name), or make a new list with them when no list matches. Use when the user asks to save targets from rank_territory, new_surgeons or warm_paths. The plan limits how many lists; up to 500 surgeons each.

tools.name: update_list_item
tools.description: Set where a listed surgeon stands (target, contacted, trialing, using_us, competitor, lost, passed) or add a note to their thread, e.g. after a call. The stage is the account's own, for the surgeon in general: it reads the same on every list and the profile, and set_account_status sets it for one pr

tools.name: log_visit
tools.description: Record a visit with a surgeon on the rep's account: a case covered, a meeting, a call, an in-service or a meal, on a date (default today), with an optional short note and the facility's CCN. Shared with the rep's team as customers are. Notes that read like patient information are refused with the re

tools.name: set_account_status
tools.description: Set where a surgeon stands in a product segment: target, contacted, trialing, using_us, competitor (with which competitor, if known), lost, passed or unknown. A surgeon can be a customer in one segment and a target in another (using us for sports medicine, not yet for shoulder), so name the segment

tools.name: set_follow_up
tools.description: Add a follow-up for a surgeon, due by a day (what to do, without patient information); close one with done and its id from my_follow_ups; or move one to another day or reword it with move, its id, and the new due or what.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Keep a note on a surgeon's account record that is not a visit: who decides, what they prefer, when to catch them, what a staff member said. Shared with the rep's team like visits, sent to a connected HubSpot as a note on the contact, and read back with the record (changes_since). For something that

tools.name: my_follow_ups
tools.description: The rep's open follow-ups (and their team's), soonest first, overdue flagged; until (YYYY-MM-DD) limits them to what is due by then, e.g. the end of this week.

tools.name: my_day
tools.description: The rep's day, as the site's Today page has it: follow-ups due, then the surgeons with a reason to call across their saved territories, their own accounts and what is new this week first, each with why and the step to take. Start a morning or a route plan here. Counts toward the plan's daily territo

tools.name: handle_reason
tools.description: Record what the rep did about a surgeon's reasons from my_day: called (off the list for 90 days), not_now (30 days) or not_relevant (for good). A new kind of reason brings the surgeon back. For a call or visit that happened, also log it with log_visit.

tools.name: my_accounts
tools.description: Every account the rep (and their team) has logged: where it stands per product segment, the share of a customer's cases held and the room to grow, when it was last touched, and the next follow-up. Filter by status or by days untouched; sort=room puts the customers with the most cases not yet won fir

tools.name: changes_since
tools.description: What changed for one surgeon since the rep last touched them (their last logged visit, status change or note; or since a given day, default 90 days): moves and practice changes, partners who joined or left, a new Open Payments year and any change of main company, a new Medicare year with the case ch

tools.name: my_customers
tools.description: The surgeons the rep already sells to, which warm_paths starts from. Give an npi to mark that surgeon a customer, or an npi with customer false to unmark them; omit both to list them.

tools.name: my_lines
tools.description: The companies the rep sells, each whole or narrowed to some brands, with the procedure families those brands cover. Other tools read these to mark switches won or lost, the rep's own recalls and their scorecard rows.

tools.name: set_my_lines
tools.description: Add a company the rep sells, optionally narrowed to some of its brands (e.g. company "Stryker", brands ["Triathlon", "Mako"]); saving a company again replaces its brands, and none means the whole company. With remove true, drop that company. Use only when the user says what they sell.

tools.name: my_territories
tools.description: The territories the rep drew and saved on MedaRep, each with a place (metro, counties, zips) to pass to rank_territory, incumbents, switching and the other territory tools, and its family when one was saved.

tools.name: save_territory
tools.description: Save a territory on the rep's MedaRep account from a metro, county FIPS codes and/or ZIP codes, optionally with its procedure family; it then shows under /territories and in my_territories. Saving under an existing territory's name replaces it. The plan limits how many territories are kept. Use only

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: update_list_item, my_accounts · Private data: new_surgeons, surgeon_profile, opportunities, log_visit, add_note, handle_reason, changes_since · Public sink: competitor_scorecard, set_account_status, my_accounts · Destructive: set_my_lines.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: update_list_item, my_accounts · Private data: new_surgeons, surgeon_profile, opportunities, log_visit, add_note, handle_reason, changes_since · Public sink: competitor_scorecard, set_account_status, my_accounts · Destructive: set_my_lines

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
